headline: The dependency bump, the three tool-call-union fixes and the new wire-parity suite are all real and verified. But the upgrade introduces a NEW boot-time regression the engineer never saw because they replaced the ticket's test scope with a providers-only run: openai 7 throws at client construction when the API key is empty, and ai/openai/chat/questions/factory.ts builds a client at module scope with `apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY || ""`. 14 existing suites in this module now fail to load without OPENAI_API_KEY. Must be fixed before publish.

verification_performed.result: CONFIRMED. Single dependency changed. Lockfile: entries 195 -> 174, 1 version change (node_modules/openai 4.87.3 -> 7.56.0), 21 entries removed, all openai-4.x-only transitives (node-fetch, form-data, agentkeepalive, ...). 0 entries added. Root dependency list identical apart from openai.

Assertions are specific: base URL + Authorization header per family, stream_options {include_usage:true}, tools/tool_choice=auto/parallel_tool_calls=true, fragmented tool-call delta reassembly, response_format json_schema + tool suppression, Azure defaultQuery api-version (default and overridden), image /images/generations with response_format b64_json. 39 = 5 families x 7 + 2 Azure + 2 normalizeCompletion. No credential or network access.

blocking_issues.title: openai 7 throws at construction with an empty API key, and factory.ts constructs a client at module scope — 14 suites now fail to load, and any key-less deployment crashes on import
blocking_issues.file: ai/openai/chat/questions/factory.ts:74 (module scope) — same pattern at factory.ts:648 and cli/reactor-cli/ReactorCli.ts:87
blocking_issues.code: export const INITIAL_CHAT_STATE: ChatState = { ... ai: new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY || "", baseURL: process.env.OPENAI_BASE_URL || "https://api.openai.com/v1" }), ... }
blocking_issues.observed_error: OpenAIError: Missing credentials. Please pass an `apiKey`, `workloadIdentity`, `adminAPIKey`, or set the `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY` environment variable. — thrown at new OpenAI (node_modules/openai/src/client.ts:631) during module evaluation of factory.ts
evidence: Direct constructor probe: openai@7.56.0 with apiKey: "" THROWS OpenAIError 'Missing credentials'; openai@4.87.3 with apiKey: "" constructs fine. This is a behaviour change of the upgrade, not of the module.

Full-scope run (--testPathPattern=reactor, no OPENAI_API_KEY): 14 suites fail to load with exactly this error — ai/macro/{support,shell,fs,chats/*,__tests__,develop}, ai/persona/__tests__/toolIncludes.contract.test.ts, services/reactor/__tests__/{ImageToolProviderResolution,ReactorProviderService.auth,.crud,.contextLength,.structuredOutput}.
Causality A: with OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-dummy-not-real the same 3 representative suites pass (104 tests).
Causality B: with openai 4.87.3 installed and NO OPENAI_API_KEY the same 3 suites pass (104 tests).
blocking_issues.impact: Not a test-only defect. Anything that imports the macro system (ai/macro/index.ts is on the normal module import path via src/modules/__index.ts in the host) evaluates factory.ts, so a process with no OPENAI_API_KEY — CI, a developer box, or a deployment that only uses azure-openai / xai / copilot / local models — now throws during module load. That is a boot-time regression for exactly the non-OpenAI provider families this ticket claims to protect.
blocking_issues.suggested_fix: Do not pass an empty string. Either construct lazily (make `ai` a getter / initialize on first use), or supply a non-empty placeholder when the key is absent (e.g. `apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY || "not-configured"`), and/or guard with `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY ? new OpenAI(...) : undefined` — the request path already fails with a clear provider error when no key is configured. Apply the same treatment to factory.ts:648 and cli/reactor-cli/ReactorCli.ts:87. Then add a regression test that imports factory.ts (or ai/macro/index.ts) with OPENAI_API_KEY unset, and re-run `--testPathPattern=reactor` as the real gate.

non_blocking_issues.title: Tool-call narrowing is stricter than the old runtime check and can silently drop tool calls from OpenAI-compatible providers that omit `type`
non_blocking_issues.detail: The old guard was `!toolCall.id || !toolCall.function`, which accepted any call carrying a `function` payload. openai 7's union only *requires* `type`, but the SDK passes provider JSON through verbatim — it does not inject `type`. With `toolCall.type !== "function"` a provider that omits the field now hits 'Invalid tool call structure' and the call is dropped; in normalizeCompletion `tc.type === "function" ? … : { name: "", arguments: "" }` turns such a call into an empty function, so dispatch fails silently instead of loudly.
non_blocking_issues.risk_note: All of the providers exercised live/wire (openai, xai, deepseek, azure) do emit type:'function'. The families with no live coverage — ollama / llamacpp / vllm and copilot — are precisely where an omitted `type` is plausible. Untested either way.
non_blocking_issues.suggested_fix: Narrow the other way round: treat everything that is not the *custom* variant as a function call, e.g. `if (!toolCall.id || toolCall.type === "custom")` in factory.ts and `tc.type === "custom" ? { name: "", arguments: "" } : { name: tc.function.name, arguments: tc.function.arguments }` in normalizeCompletion. That keeps the openai 7 types happy while preserving 4.87.3 runtime behaviour for every provider.

non_blocking_issues.title: GoogleAIService fix casts past the union instead of narrowing it
non_blocking_issues.detail: `(toolCall as { function?: ... }).function` type-checks but deliberately discards the discriminated union the other two fixes respect. Runtime behaviour equals openai 4.x (a `custom` call yields undefined function, falls through to the Google-shaped fallbacks), so this is not a defect — it is an inconsistency worth aligning for the next reader, and it hides the same omitted-`type` case as N1.

non_blocking_issues.title: The 'reasoning model omits max_tokens' matrix item is close to vacuous
non_blocking_issues.file: services/reactor/providers/__tests__/OpenAIService.wireParity.test.ts ('omits max_tokens for a reasoning model and includes it only when asked')
non_blocking_issues.detail: toOpenAIParams only sets max_tokens when config.maxTokens is a number — no model gets a default. So the first assertion (`'max_tokens' in body === false`) would pass for every model, reasoning or not. Only the control (`maxTokens: 512` -> body.max_tokens === 512) carries information. Either rename the case to say what it proves, or add a non-reasoning model to the same test so the reasoning distinction is actually asserted.

non_blocking_issues.title: Report scope substitution overstates an acceptance criterion
non_blocking_issues.detail: report.json maps `./bin/jest.sh reactory local --testPathPattern=reactor green` to a providers-only run and calls it MET. The actual pattern yields 20 failed suites / 6 failed tests. The report is otherwise unusually honest (it labels un-run families clearly), which makes this substitution the more important to correct — a reader who trusts the acceptance table would ship a red module.

non_blocking_issues.title: 3 remaining broad-suite failures are unrelated to this diff but unexplained
non_blocking_issues.detail: __tests__/unit/SchemaValidity.unit.test.ts (5 tests, GraphQL 'Unknown type JSON/User/DateTime') fails with and without an API key and has no openai involvement; ReactorConversationService.updateChatData.test.ts (OverwriteModelError, model name built from Date.now()); forms/__tests__/* (3 suites, ENOENT on a sibling worktree path src/modules/reactory-worktrees/reactory-core/forms/Widgets/...). All look environmental/pre-existing, but the engineer never ran them, so they should be confirmed against master rather than assumed.
non_blocking_issues.suggested_action: Record them as a known-red baseline for the reactor-scoped test gate so the next dependency bump is judged against a real baseline.

non_blocking_issues.title: zod was intentionally not added
non_blocking_issues.detail: The ticket's scope item 2 says 'Land openai 7.56.0 + zod 4.6.7'. The engineer did not add zod, with the justification that openai 7 declares it only as an optional peer and nothing in the module imports zod. I verified both facts (installed manifest + repo-wide grep). Accepting the deviation, but it should be stated as a deliberate deviation in the PR body so it does not read as an omission.

non_blocking_issues.detail: package.json is still @reactory/reactor 1.1.0 and nothing is published or rolled into the host, so production keeps resolving openai 4.104.0. Pipeline-owned per the run instructions, listed here so it is not lost. Also: the 39-test suite is still untracked (?? in git status) — confirm the publisher stages untracked files, or it will not ship.

acceptance_criteria_assessment.note: Agent is forbidden from touching dependabot PRs; pipeline/human action. Change is prepared on feature/6af7304df164280348fee65f.

Independently reproduced: 988 total / 737 module errors, signature-identical to the engineer's run, 0 new / 1 gone vs the 4.87.3 baseline. An absolute zero is not achievable in this module (737 pre-existing), so 'no new errors' is the correct form of this gate.
20 failed suites / 6 failed tests; 14 of those suites are a new regression caused by openai 7 (see B1). The engineer's substitute run covered only services/reactor/providers.

acceptance_criteria_assessment.criterion: One live conversation per provider family (openai, xai, copilot, azure-openai) + one local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, incl. tool-call and structured-output turns
acceptance_criteria_assessment.note: Live: xai 4/4 (text, streaming usage 213/14/547, tool call, structured output) and deepseek 3/3 (text, streaming usage 55/54/109, tool call). NOT RUN: openai (no key), copilot (no GITHUB_TOKEN), azure-openai (no key/endpoint), local ollama/vllm/llamacpp (nothing listening). Wire coverage exists for all five families but proves call shape, not server semantics. The remaining gate is real and should be an explicit pre-merge/pre-deploy step rather than folded into 'done'.

acceptance_criteria_assessment.criterion: No regression in streaming token counts / usage accounting from stream_options.include_usage
acceptance_criteria_assessment.note: Accounting was broken before the change (usage unreachable behind the choices-less final chunk). Fixed, guarded by tests that I verified fail against the pre-fix code, and confirmed live on two providers.

what_went_well: The two headline findings are genuine: the ticket's probe really did miss the function|custom tool-call union, and streaming usage really was dead. Both were root-caused precisely, and the usage fix is proven by a test that fails on the old code.

The wire-parity suite is the right instrument for this upgrade: real SDK, only fetch stubbed, no network or credentials, per-family assertions on URL, auth header, body shape and round-tripped usage. It is a real asset for the module and materially better than the existing mock-based provider tests.
Dependency hygiene is exemplary: one dependency moved, 21 obsolete transitives removed, `npm ci` verified, lockfile semantically diffed.

Un-run coverage is labelled NOT RUN with the exact reason rather than being folded into a pass. The DeepSeek tool-name pattern, the Azure Bearer-auth observation and the xAI total-vs-completion token note are useful, correctly scoped-as-pre-existing findings.
No test was weakened, skipped or deleted; the temporary live probe was cleaned up.
required_actions_next_cycle: 1 (blocking) Fix the empty-api-key construction in ai/openai/chat/questions/factory.ts (module scope, line 74), factory.ts:648 and cli/reactor-cli/ReactorCli.ts:87 — lazily initialise or use a non-empty placeholder — and add a test that imports ai/macro/index.ts (or factory.ts) with OPENAI_API_KEY unset.

2 (blocking) Re-run the real acceptance gate, `node scripts/ai/run-worktree-tests.js --testPathPattern=reactor` (or ./bin/jest.sh reactory local --testPathPattern=reactor), with OPENAI_API_KEY unset, and report the actual counts. Expect 14 suites to turn green from fix 1; record the remaining environmental reds (SchemaValidity, updateChatData, forms) explicitly.
3 (should fix in this PR) Invert the tool-call narrow to `type === "custom"` in factory.ts and OpenAIService.normalizeCompletion so providers that omit `type` keep working (N1).
4 (should fix) Correct the acceptance-criteria table in report.json: the test-path criterion is not met by a providers-only run (N4).
5 (nice to have) Align GoogleAIService's cast with the narrowing used elsewhere (N2) and make the reasoning-model max_tokens case assert something model-specific (N3).

6 (carry as an explicit gate) Live turn per remaining family (openai, copilot, azure-openai, local ollama/vllm/llamacpp) in staging, including tool-call and structured-output turns, plus publish @reactory/reactor 1.2.0 and roll it into the host.
